text: May 6th is inextricably linked with our respect and gratitude toward the invincible Bulgarian military, said Patriarch Daniil (06.05.2026 10:54)

In the tradition of Bulgarian statehood and the Church, May 6th is inextricably linked with our reverence and gratitude toward the invincible Bulgarian military. This was stated by the Bulgarian Patriarch and Metropolitan of Sofia, Daniil, who today led the solemn blessing of the waters and the consecration of the battle flags in the capital.

“In enduring testimony to the triumph of life, brought about by the Resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, I wholeheartedly congratulate you on the most radiant feast of the holy and glorious Great Martyr George—a warrior of Christ wondrous in faith and virtue, and our universally glorified heavenly intercessor and miracle-worker. Following the tradition on May 6th, the feast day of Saint George the Victorious, our holy Orthodox Church consecrates the banners of military glory of our victorious Army, beseeching God’s mercy and protection for our Orthodox military, which preserves the peace and security of our dear homeland and, with a sense of duty, watches over the lives and honor of Bulgarian citizens,” Patriarch Daniil further stated.

In his words, "our prayers and the sacred rites ordained for today's festive day have their foundation in the historically attested truth that always, in our centuries-old Orthodox tradition, the reliance of the Bulgarian military has been first and foremost on God – on Him, from Whom we know that every actual strength and power comes, as well as in our faith in Christ the Savior, which was a leading conviction not only for Christ's warrior and martyr Saint George, celebrated today by the Holy Church, but also for all Bulgarian warriors who entered battle in defense of their brothers and sisters in faith and kin."

"The sources of our people's millennial history tell us that the tradition of consecrating battle flags dates back to the First Bulgarian Kingdom, to the time of the glorious Bulgarian Tsar Simeon I the Great. The first such historically attested event is the consecration performed in 917 – before the battle at the Achelous River, which was victorious for Bulgarian arms. In the performance of this ritual, the strength of our great ancestors' reliance on God and His eternal righteousness is revealed to us; their conviction that without God and the grace-filled power flowing from Him to mankind, we can do nothing that is truly good and beneficial. Our Lord Jesus Christ tells us the same: '...he who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing,' Patriarch Daniil reminded."

„Guided by this faith and this conviction, our great ancestors of all times have sought and entreated God's help in every one of their endeavors. This is what we do today as well, when in the unity and unanimity of Church and state, we pray for God's help for our glorious military, and for peace, light, and prosperity for our people and Motherland. May the sprinkling of these battle flags with water sanctified through God's grace be yet another testimony to our faith in God and a visible sign of God's favor and protection for our entire nation, and especially for the Bulgarian servicemen who have dedicated their lives to sacrificial military service in the ranks of the Bulgarian Army,“ said the Bulgarian Patriarch.
